# Enhancement Relationship Graph

<!-- Generated by `task index` — do not edit by hand. -->

Entries are partitioned by `config.yaml.category`, the type of work. The Overview
shows how the categories lean on each other; each section shows one category
with its foreign neighbours drawn as grey stubs. Closed entries (delivered,
rejected, superseded, withdrawn) appear only where a live entry reaches them.

## Overview

One node per category, live and closed entry counts in the label. An edge label
counts the `after` edges that cross from one category into another; edges
inside a category are not shown here, and `superseded_by` is a lifecycle
relation rather than layering, so it is left to the sections.

```mermaid
graph LR
  classDef draft       fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#b45309,color:#000
  classDef accepted    fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#1d4ed8,color:#000
  classDef rejected    fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#b91c1c,color:#7f1d1d,stroke-dasharray:4 2
  classDef withdrawn   fill:#fef2f2,stroke:#b91c1c,color:#7f1d1d,stroke-dasharray:1 3
  classDef superseded  fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#6b7280,color:#6b7280
  classDef delivered   fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#15803d,color:#14532d
  classDef stub        fill:#f3f4f6,stroke:#9ca3af,color:#374151
  classDef category    fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#6d28d9,color:#000

  Cschema["schema (1 live entry, 2 closed)"]:::category
  Cruntime["runtime (1 live entry, 1 closed)"]:::category
  Cdistribution["distribution (0 live entries, 2 closed)"]:::category
  Ctooling["tooling (2 live entries, 2 closed)"]:::category
  Cmisc["misc (0 live entries, 3 closed)"]:::category

  Cschema -->|1| Cruntime
  Cschema -->|1| Cdistribution
  Cruntime -->|1| Cschema
```

Mutually dependent categories (informational; the entry-level `after` graph stays acyclic, `task vet` enforces it): schema ↔ runtime.

## Legend

```mermaid
graph LR
  classDef draft       fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#b45309,color:#000
  classDef accepted    fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#1d4ed8,color:#000
  classDef rejected    fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#b91c1c,color:#7f1d1d,stroke-dasharray:4 2
  classDef withdrawn   fill:#fef2f2,stroke:#b91c1c,color:#7f1d1d,stroke-dasharray:1 3
  classDef superseded  fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#6b7280,color:#6b7280
  classDef delivered   fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#15803d,color:#14532d
  classDef stub        fill:#f3f4f6,stroke:#9ca3af,color:#374151
  classDef category    fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#6d28d9,color:#000

  subgraph statuses ["Node statuses"]
    Ldraft["draft"]:::draft
    Laccepted["accepted"]:::accepted
    Lrejected["rejected"]:::rejected
    Lwithdrawn["withdrawn"]:::withdrawn
    Lsuperseded["superseded"]:::superseded
    Ldelivered["delivered"]:::delivered
  end

  subgraph other ["Other node kinds"]
    Lstub["NNNN · section (stub: lives in that section)"]:::stub
    Lcategory["section (n entries)"]:::category
  end

  subgraph edges ["Edge types"]
    Eaft_a["later"] -->|after| Eaft_b["earlier"]
    Esup_new["newer"] ==>|supersedes| Esup_old["older"]
    Ecat_a["category A"] -->|n| Ecat_b["category B"]
  end
```

A stub is an entry that lives in another section; its label names the section to jump to. `after` is a soft hint that an entry follows another; it blocks nothing. In the Overview, an edge label `n` counts the `after` edges crossing from A into B. Closed entries (delivered, rejected, superseded, withdrawn) appear only where a live entry's edge reaches them.
